_doc: Single source of truth for the CI bundle-size guard.
Two thresholds for core JS:
- coreJsTargetBytes: aspirational target. Exceeding it logs a
warning but does NOT fail CI. Acts as a tripwire so we notice
drift without blocking incremental UX work.
- coreJsHardLimitBytes: real ceiling. Exceeding it FAILS CI.
Set with enough headroom that day-to-day PRs don't need to
touch this file. Bump only when a deliberate decision is made
to redefine the ceiling (e.g. lazy-loading nationalPool data,
or a major data-pool addition).
Why two thresholds?
Previously every UX-polish wave bumped the same yaml line and
collided in merges. Splitting target (soft) from hard limit
(rare) means concurrent UX PRs land without conflict.
Numbers explained:
- 7.75 MB target = current main baseline after icon/UI-polish
+ squad-builder waves. Re-tune downward when we lazy-load
nationalPool.
- 9.00 MB hard limit = ~1.25 MB headroom over target. Roughly
hundreds of small UX PRs of headroom before another bump.
_eagerDoc: eagerGzHardLimitBytes: gzipped size of the FIRST-LOAD payload — the entry
chunk plus every <link rel=modulepreload> JS chunk in dist/index.html.
Checked by scripts/check-eager-bundle.mjs. This protects boot/first-paint
UX: the on-disk core-JS budget above counts lazy chunks the same whether or
not they load at startup, so it cannot catch a lazy chunk accidentally
entering the boot graph (e.g. squad-data merged into an eagerly-imported
chunk). Baseline ~485 KB gz; 560 KB hard limit leaves headroom for normal
growth while tripping on a multi-hundred-KB regression.
